github.intro: The GitHub connector completes authorization outside the sandbox. Prefer GitHub OAuth. The platform automatically creates a default profile and applies the authorization result to the current session after the callback.

steps.0: Confirm the current account, organization, and repository scope on the GitHub authorization page.
steps.1: If the GitHub App is already authorized, GitHub may jump directly back to oneceo. This is normal behavior.
steps.2: If you need broader repository scope or updated permissions, finish the authorization or installation update on GitHub and then reconnect.

tips.0: If an organization repository uses SSO, you may need to confirm it again on GitHub after authorization.
tips.1: Clearing local authorization only removes the state stored in oneceo. It does not automatically revoke the remote authorization on GitHub.

slack.intro: The Slack connector uses Composio managed authorization and MCP tool calls. oneceo keeps broker data on the API server only, without sending Slack tokens or MCP headers into the sandbox.

steps.0: Click connect and finish workspace authorization on the Composio/Slack authorization page.
steps.1: After returning to oneceo, the system saves the Slack profile and mounts it to the current session when needed.
steps.2: Session tool calls go through the API broker to Composio MCP; the sandbox receives no Slack or Composio credentials.

tips.0: Legacy Slack User OAuth profiles must be reconnected through Composio.

steps.0: Click connect and finish Supabase authorization on the Composio authorization page.
steps.1: After returning to oneceo, the system saves the Supabase profile and mounts it to the current session when needed.
steps.2: Session tool calls go through the API broker to Composio MCP; the sandbox receives no Supabase or Composio credentials.

tips.0: Legacy Supabase token profiles must be reconnected through Composio.
tips.1: Confirm the target project before schema, data, auth, storage, function, or settings changes.

composioToolkit.label: Composio Supabase toolkit
composioToolkit.description: Review the Composio managed Supabase toolkit

figma.intro: The Figma connector uses Composio managed authorization and exposes Figma capabilities through oneceo API-brokered MCP tools. Personal Access Tokens are not accepted.

steps.0: Click connect and finish the Composio/Figma authorization flow.
steps.1: After authorization, attach Figma to the current session or keep it as a reusable profile.
steps.2: The sandbox receives only brokered MCP tools; it never receives a Figma token.

tips.0: Do not paste Figma tokens into the chat, connector form, shell, or sandbox files.
tips.1: Reconnect through Composio if the Figma account or workspace access changes.

google_super.intro: The Google Workspace connector uses Composio Google Super managed authorization and exposes MCP tools through the oneceo API broker. Google tokens, Composio keys, and MCP headers are never sent to the frontend or sandbox.

steps.0: Click connect and finish the Composio/Google Workspace authorization flow.
steps.1: After authorization, attach Google Workspace to the current session or keep it as a reusable profile.
steps.2: The agent searches tools first, fetches schemas on demand, then executes through the broker. High-risk writes require one-time confirmation.

tips.0: Do not paste Google tokens, Composio API keys, MCP URLs, or headers into chat, forms, shell, or sandbox files.
tips.1: Before sending email, changing calendars, sharing files, or editing Docs/Sheets, make the target object explicit.

composioToolkit.label: Composio Google Super Toolkit
composioToolkit.description: Review the Composio-managed Google Super toolkit

vercel.intro: The Vercel connector now uses Vercel Integration installation authorization. After authorization completes, the platform calls the Vercel REST API through the oneceo internal MCP wrapper instead of exposing the official MCP endpoint or a personal token inside the sandbox.

steps.0: Click connect and finish the Vercel Integration installation flow.
steps.1: If you want a default team or project scope, fill in teamId, projectId, or projectSlug on the profile.
steps.2: After authorization, the platform mounts the profile as an internal MCP provider. The agent sees Vercel MCP tools, not a personal token.

tips.0: Use separate profiles for different teams or projects so deployment, domain, and env-var context does not get mixed.
tips.1: Before changing env vars or production-facing settings, make the target project and environment explicit.
